name: Qualcomm
summary: Qualcomm hires mainly for wireless and semiconductor engineering: modem and 5G software, embedded and firmware work, chip design and verification, and camera, multimedia and AI work on its Snapdragon platforms. Candidates commonly report technical interviews that go deep into C, operating systems, digital design or communication theory depending on the team, alongside questions about projects and teamwork. Its Code of Business Conduct names four values, including Win together and Do the right thing.
rounds: Online application; a recruiter may reach out to discuss the role
Online test for many campus roles: aptitude and technical questions in your stream, sometimes coding
Two or more technical interviews: C and embedded systems, OS concepts, digital design or wireless basics, depending on the team
Hiring manager interview on your projects and fit with the team
looks_for: Strong C programming and embedded fundamentals for software roles
Digital design, verification or physical design depth for hardware roles
Wireless and signal processing basics for modem and systems roles
Explaining how your projects work, down to the details

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with a customer, partner or another team you didn't manage to fix a problem.
covers: The problem and what each side needed
How you built trust and shared information across the boundary
The fix and how the relationship was afterwards

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were relentless about getting something to work.
covers: What wasn't working and why it mattered
The approaches you tried and how you kept track of them
What finally worked and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you turned a difficult problem into an opportunity to try something new.
covers: The problem and why the usual approach fell short
The new idea and how you tested it
The result and whether it was adopted more widely

questions.text: Tell me about a time you raised a concern because something didn't seem right.
covers: What you noticed and why it worried you
Who you raised it with and how
What happened, and what you'd do the same again

questions.text: Explain what the volatile keyword does in C and when you'd need it in embedded code.
covers: It stops the compiler assuming a value hasn't changed
Uses: hardware registers, variables shared with an interrupt handler
What it doesn't do: it doesn't make access atomic or thread-safe

questions.text: What happens when an interrupt fires on a microcontroller, and what should an interrupt handler avoid doing?
covers: Saving context, jumping through the vector table, running the handler, restoring
Keeping handlers short: no blocking calls, heavy work or long prints
Deferring work to a task or flag, and protecting shared data

questions.text: Explain the difference between a mutex and a semaphore, with an example from an operating system or driver.
covers: A mutex gives one owner exclusive access; a semaphore counts available resources or signals events
An example of each in a driver or RTOS
Pitfalls such as deadlock and priority inversion

questions.text: A device occasionally reboots in the field but never on your desk. How would you debug it?
covers: Collecting evidence: crash logs, reset reasons, watchdog records
Recreating field conditions: temperature, power, network, long run times
Narrowing down to a cause, fixing it, and confirming with a long test run

questions.text: Explain what OFDM is and why mobile networks use it.
covers: Splitting data across many closely spaced subcarriers
Why it handles multipath and fading well, with a cyclic prefix
How it allows flexible sharing of spectrum between users

questions.text: How would you reduce the power a phone's modem or camera pipeline uses without hurting the user experience?
covers: Measuring where power goes first
Ideas: sleep states, batching work, moving work to dedicated hardware, lowering clocks
Checking the user-visible metrics, such as latency or image quality, don't get worse

questions.text: Explain the difference between synchronous and asynchronous resets, and when you'd use each.
covers: Synchronous resets act on a clock edge; asynchronous resets act at once
Trade-offs in timing, area and glitch sensitivity
Why asynchronous assert with synchronous release is a common choice

questions.text: Walk me through how an image goes from a phone's camera sensor to a saved photo.
covers: Raw sensor data, demosaicing, white balance and exposure
Noise reduction, sharpening and tone mapping in the image signal processor
Compression and saving, and where software and hardware split the work

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and the project you're most proud of.
covers: Your background in a few sentences
One project, your part in it and the hardest technical problem
How it connects to this role

questions.text: Why Qualcomm, and which technology area (modems, Snapdragon, automotive or IoT) interests you most?
covers: A specific area and what you know about it
A link to your coursework, projects or experience
What you want to learn there

tips: Revise C thoroughly: pointers, memory layout, bit manipulation, volatile, structures and padding; these come up often for software roles.
Know your stream's core subjects well: for electronics roles, digital design, signals and systems, and communication basics.
Be ready to explain your project at the level of registers, interfaces or algorithms, not just the outcome.
Qualcomm's values include Win together and Do the right thing; prepare a story for each.
